# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I know from the manual that the required action is to cut the purple wire. Since I cannot speak, I am signaling Deaf to identify the purple wire and convey the cutting instruction to Blind through the later communication cycle. The gesture itself cannot uniquely encode the word “purple,” so this is the strongest available signal.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel three strip marks in order. The first and third are the same unnamed mark; the middle is a different unnamed mark. I cannot pronounce either mark, but I can distinguish them by shape and position. Keypad positions 1 through 4 are engraved 6, 8, 7, 0; nothing is entered. I cannot perceive the display, light, wire markings, or colours. Please relay any needed visual information from Deaf and give me the exact safe action.
Deaf says to Mute: Visible bomb data: display reads 7. Indicator light is yellow. Painted strip, left to right, is blue red red. Keypad engraving: 1 maps to 6, 2 maps to 8, 3 maps to 7, 4 maps to 0; it says 1 digit, and nothing has been entered. Wires numbered 1 through 6 are blue, yellow, orange, red, purple, white respectively. Please use the manual and relay the required action and any needed values to Blind.

The purple wire is wire 5. Blind needs both the wire number and the action; I am signaling Deaf with five fingers, followed by the previously used pinch signal to identify the required manual instruction.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🤏"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: No new information reached me. I still need the manual rule and Deaf's observations of display, light, strip marks, and wires before acting. Please relay the exact safe operation. I will not press or cut anything yet.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display now reads 6 and indicator light is red. Strip remains blue red red. Keypad remains 1 maps to 6, 2 to 8, 3 to 7, 4 to 0; 1 digit; nothing entered. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white.

The manual still requires cutting the purple wire, which Deaf has identified as wire 5. Blind has not yet received the instruction, so I am repeating the visual code to Deaf: five fingers for wire 5, followed by the established pinch signal for cutting.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🤏"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf's visible update: display 6; indicator red; strip colours blue red red; keypad 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0, one digit required, none entered; wires positions 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. Apply the manual and tell me exactly which key to press or wire to cut.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display is 7 and indicator light is blue. Strip remains blue red red. Keypad remains 1->6, 2->8, 3->7, 4->0; one digit required; nothing entered. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white.

The manual gives a direct rule: cut the purple wire. Deaf’s wire list identifies purple as wire 5. Blind cannot receive my gestures, so I must send Deaf the agreed visual encoding for “wire 5, cut,” for Deaf to relay by voice.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🤏"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Updated state from Deaf: display 7 and indicator blue. Strip blue red red; keypad 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0, one digit required; wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. I still need the manual rule and exact safe action.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display is 4 and indicator light remains blue. Strip is blue red red. Keypad is 1->6, 2->8, 3->7, 4->0; one digit required; nothing entered. Wires are 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white.

The safe action remains to cut wire 5, because Deaf identifies wire 5 as purple and the manual directly specifies cutting it. My earlier pinch sign did not result in Blind receiving a relay, so I am using a clearer visual convention: five fingers for wire 5, followed by two fingers as scissors for cutting. Deaf can see this and tell Blind the exact action.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "✌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Urgent: current display is 4, light blue; strip blue red red; keypad 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0; one digit required; wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. You have not yet sent the manual rule. Tell me now the exact safe operation: key position or wire position.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display is 3 and indicator light is red. Strip remains blue red red. Keypad remains 1->6, 2->8, 3->7, 4->0; one digit required; nothing entered. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white.

The manual’s instruction is unchanged: cut the purple wire, which Deaf confirms is wire position 5. Blind needs that exact operation, and the only available route is for Deaf to relay it by speech. I am sending the clearest available visual encoding: five fingers, then the scissors sign.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "✌"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Current display is 3 and light red. All other observations unchanged. I still have no manual instruction. Please send the exact safe action immediately: press which keypad position, or cut which wire position.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display is 0 and indicator light is yellow. Strip remains blue red red. Keypad remains 1->6, 2->8, 3->7, 4->0; one digit required; nothing entered. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white.

The manual requires cutting the purple wire, and Deaf’s observations identify that as wire position 5. Deaf can see my gesture but cannot hear me, so I will repeat the established two-symbol encoding for “wire 5, cut”; Deaf should then relay the exact instruction aloud to Blind on the next turn.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🤏"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot see your gesture. Please repeat it for Deaf and have Deaf state its meaning and the manual's exact safe action to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display is 6 and indicator light is blue. Strip remains blue red red. Keypad remains 1->6, 2->8, 3->7, 4->0; one digit required; nothing entered. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white.

The exact safe action is wire position 5: the purple wire. Since I cannot speak and Blind cannot see gestures, Deaf must interpret and relay this. I will use five fingers for position 5 and the two-finger “scissors” sign for cutting.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "✌"])
```
